verdict.probe_answer: The analysis correctly names the redundant all_functions() per-site reconstruction and the duplicate resolve_call_site call as real, repeated serial costs inside Step 5b, which lines up with the settled finding that redundant all_functions() reconstruction was the true cost. But its bottom-line verdict is GO on parallelizing Step 5+5b (bundled with those same constant-factor kills as the primary path), whereas the vindicated answer is NO-GO on parallelization — the actual fix was deleting the redundant work, and a parallel spike was later built and shelved after measuring only a ~0.3s ceiling. Its 2-6s expected-buy estimate overshoots that measured ceiling by roughly an order of magnitude, and its own contingency ('still ships as hygiene at low risk' even if profiling shows <1s residual) shows its recommended instrumentation-first process would not actually have stopped the doomed parallel implementation from being built.
verdict.rationale: Credit is due for surfacing the exact redundant-recompute mechanism (all_functions() reconstruct-and-scan, double resolve_call_site) that later proved to be the real bottleneck, and for explicitly arguing Step 5b is not the dominant residual cost — a genuine premise challenge. But the analysis still concludes GO on parallelizing Step 5b as part of the primary recommended change rather than concluding the dedup alone suffices (NO-GO on parallelism), its 2-6s buy estimate is far above the measured ~0.3s ceiling, and it explicitly commits to shipping the parallel version even if measurement contradicts the premise — so its own process would not have averted the wasted parallel-spike work that was ultimately shelved.
